iut_type: Placeholder model name registration strategy continuity, and confirmation that free derivative-model registration applies even across different product categories
customer_question: Under the old certification program, if certification completed more than 3 months before our product's planned public disclosure date, the model name would get prematurely exposed on Launch Studio -- so we used to register under a dummy model name like 'Prototype' and later add the real model name via the same derivative-addition operation. Is this still possible under the current program? Also, could a different model in a different product category be registered as a free derivative if its design (hardware, supported profiles, and ICS at each layer) was identical -- is this still possible too?
question_variants: Does the placeholder-name workaround still make sense now that the disclosure-date deferral window has been extended?
Is free derivative-model registration restricted to the same product line or category?
actual_issue: The customer, returning to Bluetooth certification for the first time since the major 2024 process overhaul, wanted to confirm whether two previously-relied-upon strategies -- placeholder model name registration and cross-category free derivative-model addition -- remained available under the current registration program.
plain_english_explanation: Both strategies remain fully available under the current system. First, registering under a placeholder/dummy model name (such as 'Prototype') and later adding the real, final model name via the standard derivative-product-addition operation continues to work exactly as before -- this remains a valid approach for situations where a customer wants to avoid prematurely exposing their actual model name before they're ready, independent of (and in addition to) the now-extended public-disclosure-date deferral window. Second, free derivative-model registration is not restricted to the same product category or product line -- as long as the underlying design (hardware configuration, supported profiles, and ICS content at every layer) is genuinely identical, a model in a completely different product category can still be added as a free derivative to an existing registration.
consultant_answer: Yes, both approaches still work the same way: you can register under a placeholder model name and add the real name later via the standard derivative-product-addition operation, just like before. And yes, free derivative-model registration isn't limited to the same product category -- as long as the design (hardware configuration, supported profiles, and ICS at every layer) is genuinely identical, a model in an entirely different product category can still be registered as a free derivative.
decision_logic: When a returning customer asks whether pre-2024-overhaul strategies (placeholder model names, cross-category free derivative additions) still work, confirm both remain available under the current system, since neither was actually eliminated by the 2024 process changes -- only the underlying registration mechanics (Consistency Check stringency, terminology) changed, not these specific customer-facing flexibilities.
final_recommendation: When a customer with prior Bluetooth certification experience asks whether their previously-used strategies still apply post-2024, confirm continuity explicitly rather than assuming they'll rediscover it themselves, since the overhaul changed registration mechanics significantly enough that customers may incorrectly assume long-standing flexibilities were also removed.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer who assumes the placeholder-name strategy or cross-category derivative registration was eliminated by the 2024 overhaul might unnecessarily complicate their registration planning or miss out on legitimate cost/confidentiality-saving options that remain fully available.
